selection_rule: Do not choose a substrate until identical conformance and representative workload suites run against each candidate under process, host, network, failover, backup, restore, and upgrade failure injection.

candidates.name: SQLite WAL
candidates.role: single-node reference and embedded deployment candidate
candidates.transaction_model: ACID transactions within one database file; writers serialize
candidates.coordination_scope: one host and filesystem locking domain; not a distributed lock service
strengths: simple backup and local durability model

candidates.name: PostgreSQL
candidates.role: server database candidate for a single-node service with durable concurrent workers
candidates.transaction_model: MVCC transactions, row locks, transactional DDL, SKIP LOCKED work claiming
candidates.coordination_scope: one authoritative database server or a separately qualified HA topology
strengths: transactional outbox can share business transaction
risks: HA failover semantics must be tested
SKIP LOCKED does not by itself guarantee fairness

candidates.name: MySQL InnoDB
candidates.transaction_model: ACID transactions, row-level locking, locking reads including SKIP LOCKED in supported versions
candidates.coordination_scope: one authoritative database server or a separately qualified HA topology
strengths: row-level locking and transactional local effects
risks: replication/failover and isolation differences require conformance tests

required_measurements_before_selection: identical claim, fencing, retry, deadline, cancellation, and idempotency conformance suite
multi-process and multi-host worker contention with lease expiry and stale-worker injection
process kill, host restart, database restart, failover, and network partition recovery
p50/p95/p99 claim and completion latency at declared concurrency and queue depth
throughput, lock wait, CPU, memory, WAL/binlog growth, and storage amplification
backup restore RPO/RTO and point-in-time recovery
schema migration compatibility during rolling application upgrades
retention, archival, vacuum/compaction cost and bounded storage growth
operational burden, licensing, managed-service cost, and recovery runbooks
limitations: No candidate was benchmarked in this experiment.
Documentation support is not runtime acceptance evidence.
No distributed lock, consensus, multi-node availability, or exactly-once external side effect is claimed.
A production database selection requires the target workload, deployment topology, and recovery objectives.
